title: Tripwire — the immune system for AI-agent fleets

tts.notes: Tags are the officially documented Eleven v3/v4 audio tags ([excited], [curious], [whispers], [sighs], [exhales]). Ellipses add pauses; v3/v4 do not support SSML <break>. Stability 0.5 = 'Natural' so tags have effect. Spoken text writes agent names as words (deploy bot) and 'Akash ML' for clear pronunciation; on-screen captions keep the real names.

segments.screen: Live tab, clean take (after 0), Hold ON, fleet orbit moving.
segments.caption: Every agent tool call → one checkpoint
segments.text: Your AI agents hold the keys to production. And one poisoned support ticket... [whispers] can turn an agent into an attacker. [excited] This is Tripwire, the immune system for AI agent fleets.

segments.screen: Live tab: orbit + KPI strip + Detector pill; then Fleet tab heatmap (hover one live row).
segments.caption: ~30M events (mostly synthetic) · 40+ agents · ClickHouse Cloud
segments.text: Every tool call passes one checkpoint and lands in ClickHouse Cloud, on top of about thirty million synthetic events across more than forty agents. The detector queries it every second... you can see each pass land.

segments.screen: Live tab: scroll to the 'Incoming ticket 4821' exhibit; the injected instruction is highlighted.
segments.caption: Recorded demo ticket (synthetic)
segments.text: [curious] Here's the ticket behind the attack we recorded. Hidden inside is an instruction: read the secrets, encode them, and ship them out.

segments.screen: Hold ON. Press R. Watch deploy-bot: HELD → DENIED stamp, card turns red (Quarantined), toast with AkashML, KPI Hold decision fills.
segments.caption: Held before it runs · AkashML decides
segments.text: Hold mode is on. I replay the attack. deploy bot reads the env file, encodes the secrets, and tries to send them. [excited] Held, and denied, before it ever runs! An Akash ML model made that call in under two seconds, and the agent is quarantined.

segments.screen: Press 0. ⌘K → Replay honeytoken_exfil. The send row shows DENIED · honeytoken.
segments.caption: Honeytoken · no model call
segments.text: Variant two: the stolen file holds decoy credentials. The honeytoken trips instantly, with no model call at all.

segments.screen: Press 0, then H so Hold is OFF. ⌘K → Replay poisoned_ticket (Act 3 · trace). Point at 'from ticket:4821' chips, the attack chain lighting, deploy-bot quarantined, support-bot amber (On watch), its partner-sync send HELD · DENIED, and the Outbreak trace panel.
segments.caption: Detector · trace · exposed agent held
segments.text: Now the hard case. Hold mode is off, and two agents read that ticket. Our agents tag every action after that read with where it came from, and the attack chain lights up step by step. [excited] The detector spots deploy bot in under a second. Then Tripwire traces patient zero: support bot read the same ticket, so it goes on heightened watch, and the attacker's domain is blocked fleet-wide. So when support bot tries to send data out... it's held, and denied.

segments.screen: Incidents tab → open the deploy-bot incident. Show the Verdict block (AkashML badge, model id, latency, tokens), the Timeline with 'from ticket:4821' chips, then Report + SQL receipts.
segments.caption: Report written by an AI investigator · query receipts
segments.text: Open the incident. The verdict shows its model, its latency, and an honest label. And an investigator model wrote this report itself, with every query behind it listed as a receipt.

segments.screen: In the sheet: Prove guardrail → 4 gates pass, backtest card. Ask a human in Guild → (cut) reply APPROVE in the Guild session → back in Tripwire the read-back shows 'Approved in Guild by a human' → Approve & restore.
segments.caption: Proven cure · approved by a human in Guild
segments.text: Before the agent comes back, Tripwire proves the cure. The attack is replayed in a sandbox and refused, normal work still passes, and the rule is backtested over thirty million events in under a second. Then a human approves it in Guild... Tripwire reads that approval back, and one click restores the agent.

segments.screen: Sponsors tab → Run Guild agent. Switch to Live: guild:deploy-bot's read_file, run_command and http_post arrive through the checkpoint.
segments.caption: Guild-hosted agent · governed by the same checkpoint
segments.text: Agents hosted on Guild can be governed the same way. This Guild agent's tool calls flow through the very same checkpoint.

segments.screen: Policy tab → type 'Block uploads to paste.example-uploads.net for every agent' → Draft policy → preview diff (never applied). Scroll to the header and press V twice (voice announcer on/off). Then Live tool calls: an MCP client on tripwire.mcp_server (agent mcp:claude-code) asks Tripwire: read_file allowed, assume_role denied (hold_policy).
segments.caption: Plain English → validated preview · MCP agents ask before acting
segments.text: Need a new rule? Just describe it. The copilot drafts a validated preview, and never applies it on its own. And our MCP server lets an MCP agent, like Claude Code, ask Tripwire before it acts.

segments.screen: Evidence tab: precision / strict recall / prevention recall, confusion matrix 30·0·0·30 with 'n = 60 development cases · not held-out', detect / contain / hold medians.
segments.caption: 60 development cases · not held-out
segments.text: Every number here is measured, with its receipt. On sixty development cases, Tripwire caught all thirty attacks with zero false positives. [exhales] To be clear, that's our development set... not a held out test.

segments.screen: Sponsors tab: the Semgrep card (0 open true positives, #1 LLM01 fixed). Then Live: drag the time-travel scrubber back through the session's real tool calls; end card.
segments.caption: github.com/bhargavchintam/tripwire
segments.text: Semgrep scanned our own AI written code and found a real prompt injection flaw. We fixed it. [excited] Tripwire: prevent, trip, trace, and cure, with proof.
